name: Hiram Everts, High School for Young Gentlemen

proprietors.name: Everts, Hiram
proprietors.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card everts_hiram (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

staffing.principal_is: Hiram Everts, this record's proprietor, whose testimonials from Professor Whitman of the Hamilton Institution were shown at a private house in Chicago.

hands.basis: period_convention, off the staffing model's `school` class, whose own row reads `schoolteacher` — the same office under the business layer's word for it: an assistant at the larger schools only, and the model's typical is 0 because the town's schools of 1835 are one room and one teacher. Its analogue is the 1839 list's thirteen schoolteachers, four years and some three thousand people after the scene.
hands.why_not_drawn: No source reached names a second person teaching for Everts, and the school had not yet opened at the scene date for one to teach in.

attendance.basis: NO FIGURE IS PRINTED, AND THE SCHOOL ITSELF WAS CONDITIONAL: Everts 'will [open a] HIGH SCHOOL for Young Gentlemen [on] the 10th of the present month, SHOULD SUFFICIENT ENCOURAGEMENT BE OFFERED'. What the notice prints is a fee scale — $5 a term of eleven weeks for the ordinary English branches, $6 for the higher, $8 for Latin and Greek. THIS SCHOOL WAS NOT STANDING ON 1 JULY 1835: the register carries it `present_at_scene_date: false` under `opening_announced_after_scene_date`, and its opening is dated 10 August 1835.

staffing.basis: THE TEACHER OF A ONE-ROOM SCHOOL IS THE PERSON WHO KEEPS IT, and this record already names them. The staffing model gives the class one role, an assistant, at 0–0–1 with a typical of nought; drawing one here would put a second schoolteacher in a room the model says held one. So the answer to 'who taught here' is a pointer at a row this record carries, not a new row beside it.
staffing.replaceable_by: Any printing that names a second person teaching at this school — an assistant, an usher, a monitor — would draw the hand above. A roll, a quarterly return or a subscription list would give the attendance a figure for 1835 instead of a silence.

locations.basis: The register resolved no place for this house at the scene date.
locations.limit_reason: Excluded from the scene-date town: chicago_democrat_1835_08_12#c006 announces this house opening on 1835-08-10, after the scene date — “he will [open a] HIGH SCHOOL for Young Gentlemen [on] the 10th of the present month”. The advertisement is dated 5 August 1835, so 'the present month' is August and the school opens on 10 August 1835 — and only 'should sufficient encouragement be offered'. It was not open on 1 July. No action; the record is kept so the exclusion can be argued with.
